utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. Before we start, I would like to turn to Mrs. Lindsay and to tell us in which capacity she is here with us today.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: I'm here today as a legal consultant to Mr. Tansey, who is now lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Would you please repeat again.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: I am here as legal consultant. I have been appointed to the Momir Nikolic team as a legal consultant, assisting Mr. Tansey, who is lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may participate as a part of the team, of course, but as you know, you are not entitled to take the floor. Thank you. [Interpretation] This being said, I would like to ask Mr. Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-60/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, can you hear and understand our proceedings? Mr. Nikolic, let me repeat: Can you hear and understand these proceedings? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, I don't seem to be receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There seems to be some technical problems here. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may sit down. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have the appearances, please, starting with the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KIND
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution today is myself, Marie-Ursula Kind, together with my colleague Mr. Mathias Marcussen, and our case manager Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now turn to Mr. Nikolic's Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appear today on behalf of Mr. Nikolic and, as you know, Ms. Virginia Lindsay is my legal consultant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you very much, Mr. Tansey. And I would like to welcome you to this Tribunal before which, if I'm not mistaken, you are appearing for the first time. Since the beginning of the appeals proceeding in this case we've been faced with a certain number of difficulties, but I am confident that from now on the parties will be able to proceed more diligently and to overcome those difficulties and to help us, obviously, overcome these problems. As you know, in keeping with the provisions of Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a status conference shall be convened within 120 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last status conference, to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including issues related to his health status, mental and physical health. This is the fourth status conference convened over the course of this appeals proceeding. Mr. Nikolic, or his Defence counsel, would you like to raise with the Chamber concerns relating to your detention, or your health status? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to tell you that I do not have any specific matters to raise in relation to my detention. The situation is quite correct and I've had some difficulties, some health problems that I am dealing with at the infirmary that is with the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. Now, regarding the appeals proceeding, the Appeals Chamber has received all briefs from the various parties in their corrected and public versions. In this particular instance, the Appeals Chamber has been -- has received three motions filed by the Defence. A motion for judicial notice, which was filed on October the 11th, 2004. I would like to inform both parties that the decision related to this motion will be issued in the coming days. A second motion for leave to file an amended notice of appeal, as well as a second motion to admit additional evidence, were also submitted to the Appeals Chamber. In a decision dated March 8th, 2005 I granted Mr. Nikolic an extension of time to file his replies to two motions. Mr. Tansey, since these motions were filed by Mr. Nikolic's former counsel, could you please tell me if your client intends to maintain these motions and to file his replies, or if, alternatively, he wishes to withdraw these motions. You have the floor, Mr. Tansey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position is that I saw Mr. Nikolic for the first time this morning. I, in fact, have had approximately two hours' consultation with him. There are many matters which, it seems, that I have to raise with him about the totality of the case and about the matters raised in the appeal, and the position is that I am nowhere near ready to deal with those particular matters. It would be foolish of me to seek to deal with those matters until I am fully conversant with all the facts of the case, as well as the law, et cetera. So the position is, at present, I cannot answer Your Honour's questions because they are matters which I have to consult with Mr. Nikolic very carefully upon. And if I may just add to that, that, as Your Honour knows, I was only instructed in this matter in around mid-February. And I have spent some considerable time already reading the background material to this case. The position is I am nowhere near ready yet to adequately advise and consider the matters raised. And yesterday -- and I don't know whether Your Honour in fact received a motion which I believe was incorrectly filed or attempted to be filed by me yesterday -- and if I may just indicate to Your Honour the nature of the motion, and it was a second motion to enlarge time for filing of replies relating to the appellant's second motion to admit additional evidence and a motion for leave to file second amended notice of appeal. Your Honour, I'm sorry if Your Honour does not or has not yet received a copy of this. I, and I alone, must take the responsibility, and that is my responsibility and my fault. But Your Honour, one certainly was filed, I believe, a short while ago at the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Tansey. Thank you for providing these explanations to me. As I said, both motions were received. I asked you if you wanted to maintain those motions or if you wanted to withdraw them before the Appeals Chamber. I've duly noted your explanations. So we still have those two motions for the time being. And the replies should be filed by April 11th, 2005 at the latest. This is where we stand now. Are we in agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My legal officer has just indicated that we have not received yet your motion asking for an extension of time limits. When we receive such motion, we will act accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: As I said, I do apologize. It is our mistake. And if I may bring to Your Honour's attention what in fact we are seeking, so that the Chamber is well aware of the issue. What in fact we are asking is for additional time to be provided to enable us to consider all these matters, and the time up to and including the 6th of June. Your Honour, I appreciate that this is a case which is of some length. It's been going -- the appeal has been going on for some time, however due to my commitments as they have been and are, and also due to the need to really master all the facts of this case, I believe that if you were to allow the date the 6th of June, then certainly we would be ready to deal with all the matters as Your Honour has asked me about and which the Court has to consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to reiterate, Mr. Tansey, we have duly noticed your explanation, we have taken due notice of your explanation, we thank you for your submissions regarding the motion that you are going to file regarding an extension of delays up until the 6th of June. This motion, when we receive it, we shall statuate [as interpreted] on the motion. This being said, I have no further observations to make with respect to this pre-trial conference. I would, however, like to ask the parties if they have any observations to make or do they have any questions to raise at this stage? Mr. Tansey, I'm turning to you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further observations at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Mrs. Marie-Ursula Kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KIND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, the Prosecution has nothing further to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam. Since there are no further questions to be dealt with at this present stage, this hearing stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.37 p.m.
